data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war.
Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days.
But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal.
"They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously.
"They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: China pushes back against US on Iran and Cuba in UN speech
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
China pushes back against US on Iran and Cuba in UN speech
China pushed back against the United States in its speech at the UN General Assembly on Saturday, saying sovereignty of countries in the Gulf should be respected and urging the "relevant country" to stop threatening Cuba and lift its blockade on it.
Vice President Han Zheng did not mention the US by name in his remarks. The US has launched a pressure campaign on Cuba that has largely blocked oil from reaching the island. The US war on Iran started with US-Israeli strikes in February.
The comments stood in sharp contrast to the bonhomie on display earlier this week at the White House, where President Donald Trump feted Chinese leader Xi Jinping with military flyovers and at a lavish state dinner.
"Major countries should have special responsibilities for safeguarding international peace and security, and they should take the lead in complying with the rules, upholding the rule of law and doing what's right," Han said.
"China holds that the sovereignty and security of countries in the Middle East, including the Gulf, should be respected."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Haftar's forces execute 30 after secret military trials in eastern Libya
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Haftar's forces execute 30 after secret military trials in eastern Libya
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Sat, 09/26/2026 - 13:13
Amnesty International says defendants were tortured into giving 'confessions' later used as evidence, as 50 more face death
Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar leaves after talks with Greece's foreign minister in Athens, on 17 January 2020 (Aris Messinis/AFP)
Off
At least 30 men have been executed in eastern Libya since late August after being sentenced to death in secretive military trials and at least 50 others remain at imminent risk of execution, local media and rights groups have reported over the last week.
Amnesty International said the Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), led by eastern commander Khalifa Haftar and the de facto authorities in the region, resumed executions on 23 August in Libya for the first time since 2010.
Those executed had been convicted following “grossly unfair and secretive trials” marred by torture, the rights group said.
Some of those executed or still awaiting death sentences were convicted of murder and terrorism-related offences linked to fighting between the LAAF and opposing armed groups between 2014 and 2018, Amnesty said.
Several detainees claimed to have been tortured by armed groups affiliated with the LAAF following their arrests, including to obtain “confessions” that were later used as evidence against them, the rights group said.
“The LAAF authorities must immediately halt all executions,” the organisation said, calling for a moratorium and the overturning of convictions and death sentences handed down following unfair trials.
Amnesty also called on authorities to retry civilians accused of internationally recognised criminal offences in accordance with international standards of fairness in civilian courts that do not use evidence obtained through torture.
It called on authorities to grant international monitors access to Gernada and other detention sites in eastern Libya.

data.title: Middle East Eye: At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping
Saudi Arabia warned UN members Saturday that attempts to block Middle East waterways are a threat to global energy security and demanded the international community do more to defend freedom of navigation.
Since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, Tehran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while its Houthi allies in Yemen have subsequently done the same in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Both waterways are vital routes for oil and gas exports.
"The international community has been absent from assuming its responsibilities in confronting all that threatens international peace and security," Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan told the United Nations General Assembly.
"The kingdom stresses the importance of guaranteeing the protection of freedom of navigation in all international waterways, foremost among them the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden," he said.

"The day after the US president's speech, it was our turn to speak. In effect, he threatened to wipe Iran off the map and labelled us as 'terrorist'," he said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel's attorney general orders postponement of E1 settlement tender
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israel's attorney general orders postponement of E1 settlement tender
Israel’s attorney general has ordered a one-month postponement of an E1 settlement construction tender in the West Bank to avoid it being used for electioneering, Al Jazeera reported.
The tender, published on 18 August, covers seven residential compounds containing 1,234 housing units, out of the 3,401 units approved for E1, according to Israeli media. The deadline for bids had been set for 19 October, eight days before the Knesset election.
E1 (East 1) would link Ma’ale Adumim and other illegal Israeli settlements to occupied East Jerusalem, effectively severing the West Bank and disrupting Palestinian movement between the northern and southern West Bank, and isolating communities on each side.
The European Union has said the E1 settlement project fundamentally undermines the prospects for a two-state solution.
It noted that these developments come amid increasing instability in the West Bank and record levels of settler violence.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Settlers smash cars, damage ambulance in West Bank village
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Settlers smash cars, damage ambulance in West Bank village
Israeli settlers smashed cars and hurled rocks at Palestinian residents of al-Mughayyir village in the occupied West Bank while Israeli forces looked on, according to a video shared by Palestinian rights activist Ihab Hassan on X.
Masked Israeli settler terrorists attacked the village of Al-Mughayyir in the West Bank today, in front of and under the protection of the Israeli border police. pic.twitter.com/iUMr72HIex
— Ihab Hassan (@IhabHassane) September 26, 2026
Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli forces, also attacked an ambulance and stole agricultural equipment during a raid on al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, on Saturday evening, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
Al-Mughayyir Village Council head Amin Abu Alia told Wafa that the settlers also raided a sheep farm west of the village and stole agricultural equipment.
During the attack, Israeli forces raided a house in the western part of the village, searched it and tampered with its contents. The forces also fired tear gas grenades in the area, with no injuries reported.
Abu Alia said Israeli forces also briefly detained several citizens, including women and children, at the village's western entrance and subjected them to mistreatment, before releasing them.
Israeli settler terrorists attacked a Palestinian ambulance while paramedics were trying to reach and treat people injured in a settler attack on the village of Al-Mughayyir in the West Bank. pic.twitter.com/2jI8T0qRvU
— Ihab Hassan (@IhabHassane) September 26, 2026
